title: Unauthenticated GET /static/novnc/* runs docker create plus a full image tar extraction on every request while the marker file is missing, with no single-flight
description: api.py:355-363 registers GET /static/novnc/{path:path} with no principal, session or ticket and calls box.sandboxes.extract_novnc(novnc_dir) on every request before it even validates the requested path. extract_novnc (sandbox_desktop.py:146-169) has one guard: it returns True if dest/core/rfb.js already exists. While that marker is absent, each request runs self.client.containers.create(desktop_image, ...), joins get_archive("/usr/share/novnc") fully into memory and extractall()s it into the control plane's data directory, then removes the container. There is no lock, no in-flight marker and no negative cache, so concurrent requests all miss the guard, duplicate the daemon work and extract into the same destination; the losing extractions raise an uncaught FileExistsError/OSError, which extract_novnc does not handle because it catches only ImageNotFound, NotFound and APIError (153-159), and the request becomes a 500.
root_cause: An unauthenticated static-asset route performs Docker-daemon work and an archive extraction behind a check-then-act test on a single marker file, with no lock or in-flight flag, and any non-docker exception escapes as a 500 that leaves the marker absent, so the work is repeatable by any anonymous client.
intended_behavior: Static assets should not require per-request daemon work: the extraction should happen once (at startup or on the first authenticated desktop use) under a lock that lets one caller do it while others wait or observe the result, and a failed extraction should leave a bounded negative state instead of being retried by every request.

trace.description: The route has no Depends() at all and is exempt from the cookie/header principal used everywhere else, so it is reachable by any network client.

The handler calls box.sandboxes.extract_novnc(novnc_dir) before resolving or validating path, so the only thing that keeps a request cheap is the marker file the function itself is supposed to create.

trace.scope: the sole guard is a marker-file existence check
trace.description: if (dest / "core" / "rfb.js").exists(): return True - a check-then-act test with no lock, no in-flight marker and no negative cache, so N concurrent callers all proceed.

Each request that finds no marker creates a container from the desktop image (152), pulls the whole /usr/share/novnc tar into memory with b"".join(stream) (156-157) and extracts it into settings.home (166), then removes the container (161).

evidence.description: Only ImageNotFound/APIError are caught around create and only NotFound/APIError around get_archive (158-159); the tarfile extraction at 163-166 is outside any handler, so FileExistsError/OSError from a concurrent or partial extraction escapes as a 500.
The final (dest.parent / "novnc").rename(dest) runs without checking whether the destination already exists.
The path-safety check and the 404 for a missing asset happen only after the extraction attempt, so even a 404 can cost a container create.
novnc_dir = settings.home / "novnc": the extraction writes into the control plane's persistent data directory.

conditions.description: The desktop image is present (otherwise create raises ImageNotFound and the route is cheap) and home/novnc/core/rfb.js is absent: a fresh install before anyone opened a desktop page, or a state left behind by a failed or partial extraction.
Two or more requests must be in flight together to duplicate the daemon work and reach the destination race; a single request duplicates nothing.
None - the route requires no principal, cookie or ticket.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated client issues GETs to /static/novnc/core/rfb.js (or any path under that prefix) instead of relying on a real user opening the desktop page, so the first-time extraction happens under its timing.
payloads: GET /static/novnc/core/rfb.js  (no headers, no cookie) - six copies issued concurrently
GET /static/novnc/does-not-exist.js  (no headers, no cookie) after deleting the extracted tree
instructions: In the approved sandbox, build the app with the Docker client replaced by an in-process fake that counts containers.create calls and serves a fixed tar containing novnc/core/rfb.js (the sandbox has no daemon).
Delete home/novnc, issue one GET, then a second GET, then six GETs with asyncio.gather, recording status codes and the number of containers.create calls.
Delete home/novnc again and issue three sequential GETs for a non-existent asset, recording creates and status per request.
execution.observed_result: With home/novnc deleted, one unauthenticated GET returned 200 with 1 containers.create call and wrote novnc/core/rfb.js; the next GET made 0 create calls (marker hit). After deleting home/novnc again, six concurrent unauthenticated GETs made 6 containers.create calls: one returned 200 and five returned 500 with FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: '<home>/novnc/core'. Three further unauthenticated GETs for a non-existent asset, each preceded by deleting the tree, made 3 more create calls and returned 404 each time while the marker stayed absent. In a separate consolidated run whose archive was deliberately truncated, every one of three unauthenticated GETs made another containers.create call and returned 500 OSError: unexpected end of data, showing that any extraction failure leaves the marker absent and the daemon work repeatable.

remediation.strategy: Extract once, under a lock, outside the request path: do it at startup or on the first authenticated desktop route, guard it with a per-directory lock plus an in-flight event so concurrent callers wait, extract and only then publish the marker, and treat any failure as a bounded negative state. /static/novnc/* should answer 404/503 without creating containers when the marker is absent.

code_changes.fixed_code:
self.client = docker.from_env()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._novnc_lock = threading.Lock()   # single-flight for extract_novnc

likelihood.reason: The expensive state is the missing marker, which exists on a fresh install and after any failed extraction; once the marker exists the cost drops to zero, so the attacker has to arrive before the first legitimate desktop use or exploit a broken state.

impact.reason: Unauthenticated Docker-daemon work, control-plane threads and data-directory writes, plus 500s and a possibly half-written asset tree; no data disclosure or privilege gain and the cost per request is bounded by one container create plus one asset-tree tar.

confidence.reason: The source trace is complete and the duplication and race were reproduced locally with the Docker client stubbed; only the daemon-side wall time of one containers.create is deployment-specific.
